nodes.label: Accessible Reordering Traceability Gap
nodes.rationale: The earlier graph showed backend reorder operations and tests but no graph path from the accessibility requirement to frontend controls or accessibility coverage.

nodes.label: Motion Accessibility Traceability Gap
nodes.rationale: The earlier graph did not connect the motion accessibility plan to the existing reduced-motion implementation.

nodes.label: Production Hardening Evidence Gap
nodes.rationale: Health checks, backups, monitoring, retries, and queued mail were absent from the graph and require source verification before being treated as missing functionality.

nodes.label: Mobile Three.js Performance Tradeoff
nodes.rationale: Skipping the Three.js scene on small screens would improve the landing page's mobile score and responsiveness, but the scene is central to the landing page's visual personality, so the decision remains open.

nodes.label: Definition-Driven Admin CMS
nodes.rationale: Central resource definitions let routes, validation, index tables, and forms share one declaration, avoiding ten near-identical controllers and reducing the work needed to add another content type.

nodes.label: Keyboard-Accessible Reordering
nodes.rationale: Up and down buttons were chosen over drag-and-drop because buttons work with keyboards and touchscreens, can expose item position, restore focus, and announce results through a live region.

nodes.label: Stable Resume Delivery Route
nodes.rationale: Serving the resume through GET /resume keeps the public link stable across re-uploads, gives the download a meaningful filename, and avoids Media Library absolute-URL failures when APP_URL omits the serving port.

nodes.label: Durable Contact Message Handling
nodes.rationale: Messages are stored before or alongside email so an SMTP failure cannot lose a job or booking enquiry; mail failure is logged without misleading the sender.

nodes.label: Single MySQL Database
nodes.rationale: Using MySQL 8.4 as the sole database removes the silent SQLite-versus-MySQL split and gives development and tests the same column, JSON, and constraint behavior expected in production.

nodes.label: Test Database Isolation
nodes.rationale: The suite pins only the portfolio_test database name through both PHPUnit env and server variables, protecting development content while allowing host and container connections to use their different network endpoints.
